evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors can be implemented independently; no concrete story in the backlog is required first.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Viewing user profiles inherently requires user accounts/profiles to exist, which depends on the registration story.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Emailing trainers requires trainer accounts/contact details to exist (user registration), which depends on the registration story.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: Providing a map is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Editing a training node presupposes authenticated trainer accounts/ability to own nodes (user registration), which depends on registration.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint presupposes a registration and authentication feature; it therefore depends on user registration being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status requires the registration/attendance data to exist (user registration/registration feature).

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: A waitlist is part of the registration workflow for trainings; it therefore depends on the training registration feature (training pages/register flow).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Acceptance of cancellation terms is part of the registration/cancellation workflow and depends on that workflow being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: This story explicitly depends on an existing registration/cancellation workflow (registration feature) being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: The feature explicitly depends on a schedule feature being present (the schedule viewing/population stories).

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Showing trainings a user signed up for requires a registration subsystem and training registration links to exist.

evaluations.evidence: view that is attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: This view requires training nodes and attendee/registration data to exist (training node creation/editing and registration).

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Building this admin view requires training sessions and registration data to exist (training pages/registration).

evaluations.evidence: have a dedicated page for each class
evaluations.rationale: Creating dedicated class pages is self-contained and does not require another specific backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: training options clearly marked ... link to full details ... register now link
evaluations.rationale: Listing training options and marking details can be implemented independently; although it mentions registration links, it is a standalone listing feature.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page with an intro section and a list of all training offerings
evaluations.rationale: A landing page listing trainings is self-contained and doesn't inherently require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link on the home page is implementable independently of other stories.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Providing location/time for the coding lounge is self-contained and does not require another story.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding money requires payment processing and recorded payments to exist (payment checkout stories).

evaluations.evidence: find a link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Placing a link to become a sponsor can be implemented independently of the backend payment flow.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Showing attendees associated with a company requires attendees to have been linked to sponsors (linking feature).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Paying for a company sponsorship requires payment/checkout infrastructure and payment processing stories to exist.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Venue CRUD (create and maintain) is a self-contained administrative feature.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details presupposes venue data created/maintained by admins, which depends on the venue creation story.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Listing sessions associated with sponsor attendees requires attendees to be linked to sponsors, which depends on a linking feature.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page to pay for my individual sponsorships as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: A payment page as part of registration depends on the registration workflow existing (registration feature).

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors to events is an admin operation and can be implemented independently given event and sponsor data.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: This view requires sponsors to have been assigned to events (assignment feature) before it can show anything.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Implementing a payment entry/charge flow is a standalone feature in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Linking attendees to a sponsorship page requires attendees (user accounts) to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating a user profile requires a user account to exist (registration), so it depends on the registration story.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: A newsletter sign-up can be implemented independently and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Tagging requires blog posts to exist, which depends on the story for creating blog posts.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a self-contained content-authoring feature.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog requires blog posts to exist (created by the blog post story).

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit typically requires the sponsorship/payment flow to be available (payment/sponsorship stories).

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Registering for a summit requires a registration capability and user accounts to exist.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Providing detailed directions depends on venue information being available (venue creation/maintenance).

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: This requires summit registration data to exist (registration story).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing summit attendees depends on the registration feature and registrations having been made.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Providing a summit coordinator the ability to list summit info is a self-contained authoring feature.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors for a summit requires sponsors to have been assigned to that summit (sponsor assignment story).

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Providing an agenda is self-contained content functionality and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Displaying remaining seats requires counting registrations/capacity, which depends on the registration/scheduling features.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: Viewing summit details requires the summit information to have been created (summit info story).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A public list of summits depends on summit entries existing, which relies on summit creation/coordination stories.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Providing sponsorship level information is standalone content and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Adding a WYSIWYG editor is a self-contained functionality for content editing.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link from job listings to a sponsorship profile can be implemented without other backlog dependencies.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Providing informational content and contact details is self-contained.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Creating the job-posting capability is a standalone feature; it does not require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board requires job postings to exist, which depends on the job posting story.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location, so that I can populate the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Populating the schedule by assigning rooms/times is an administrative feature that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: This notification depends on the session submission feature which generates the trigger for the notification.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing a session presupposes a session has been submitted (session submission feature).

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp
evaluations.rationale: Registering to speak implies a session submission/registration mechanism; it depends on the session submission feature.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session requires an authenticated user account; the registration/authentication story must exist to support this.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Personalizing a sponsorship page requires that the sponsor/sponsorship account exists (payment/registration of sponsor).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a list of summits requires summit entries to exist (summit creation/listing by coordinators).

evaluations.rationale: Offering sponsorship choices as part of registration depends on the registration/payment checkout and payment pages being implemented.

evaluations.rationale: Adding a menu link is an independent UI change and does not inherently require other backlog stories.

evaluations.rationale: Implementing user registration is a base capability and is not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Providing session information lookup is self-contained and does not inherently require another story.
